SOURCE: Porter Sargent Publishers, "The Guide to Summer Camps and Summer Schools",
        1983-1984 (23rd edition) and December 1987.
        Internet Archive items guidetosummercam0000unse (1983-84, scan leaf 484) and
        guidetosummercam0000port (1987, scan leaf 478).
        Both lending-restricted; NEITHER can be read from here. Assembled 2026-09-06 from
        overlapping Open Library search-inside windows. RECONSTRUCTIONS, not transcriptions.

The two entries are near-identical in wording, which is normal for an annual guide reprinting a
camp's standing return. Where a window returned both books at once, the differences between them
are noted.

=== 1983-84 EDITION ===

  KANAWANA  189 Boys and Girls  7-15
  St. Sauveur des Monts, Quebec. Est. 1894. Peter G. Goddard, Montreal Y.M.C.A.,
  1441 Drummond St., Quebec H3G 1W5. $380 2 wks. Tents. Cabins. C.I.T.
  Canoe tripping is featured and trips range from 2 mile hikes to 100 mile wilderness canoe
  trips through northern Quebec according to age and ability of campers. In-camp activities
  [...] canoeing, archery and crafts. In The Voyageurs Program, 14-day wilderness canoe tripping
  is featured for teenagers 13-18.
  [and, from a window returning both editions:] "multicultural living experience for French and
  English speaking children. Bilingual instruction program available."

=== 1987 EDITION ===

  KANAWANA  190 Boys and Girls  7-15
  St. Sauveur des Monts, Quebec JOR 1RO. Est. 1894. Jay Netherwood, Montreal Y.M.C.A.,
  1441 Drummond St. [...] wks. Extras $20. Tents. Cabins. C.I.T.
  Canoe tripping is featured and trips range from 2-mile hikes to 100-mile wilderness canoe
  trips through northern Quebec according to age and ability of campers. In-camp activities
  [...] In The Voyageurs Program, 14-day wilderness canoe tripping is featured for teenagers
  13-18.

WHAT WAS NOT RECOVERED: the 1987 fee figure (the window begins mid-field at "wks. Extras $20");
the full In-camp activities list in either edition; and whatever precedes "canoeing, archery and
crafts". Both books also carry Kanawana in a cross-reference index of Canadian camps and in an
index of camps by state and country, neither of which was read.
